title: Guess the Number
blurb: Guess the number the computer picked
intro: This time it's a number guessing game! The computer secretly picks a number from 1 to 50, and you keep guessing with "Too high" and "Too low" hints until you get it. The while loop from Chapter 5 is the star.
finale: You did it! Want to see who can guess it in fewer tries, you or me? If you keep cutting the range in half, you'll always get it within six guesses.

steps.goal: Let the computer secretly pick an answer

tool.title: New tool: random.randint
tool.body: random is a toolbox of chance that comes with Python. Write import random once at the top of your code to use it. random.randint(1, 6) picks one number from 1 to 6. Both ends, 1 and 6, can come up.

steps.task: The starter code already has import random. Below it, store a number from random.randint(1, 50) in answer (call random only once, on this line). Then print "I picked a number from 1 to 50". Don't show the answer yet.

hints: random.randint(start, end) includes both start and end. For 1 to 50, use those two numbers as they are.
The number it picks is the answer you'll guess later, so keep it under the name answer.

import random

answer = random.randint(___, ___)
print("I picked a number from 1 to 50")
steps.solution:
import random

answer = random.randint(1, 50)
print("I picked a number from 1 to 50")
steps.explain: randint(1, 50) picks one number, and 1 and 50 are both possible. The answer is only stored in answer, not shown. Now it's time to guess.

steps.task: At the bottom, read a number with int(input()) into guess. If guess equals answer, print "Correct!"; otherwise print "Nope".

hints: input() gives you text. The text "37" and the number 37 are different, so wrap it in int() to compare it with answer.
To ask whether two things are equal, use two equals signs ==, not one.
steps.solution:
import random

answer = random.randint(1, 50)
print("I picked a number from 1 to 50")
guess = int(input())
if guess == answer:
    print("Correct!")
else:
    print("Nope")
steps.explain: input() gives text, so int() turns it into a number before comparing with == to answer. Without int, "37" never equals 37 and you always see "Nope".

steps.task: Give a hint instead of "Nope". Where else was, add elif guess > answer: and print "Too high", then in the last else print "Too low".

steps.solution:
import random

answer = random.randint(1, 50)
print("I picked a number from 1 to 50")
tries = 0
while True:
    guess = int(input())
    tries += 1
    if guess == answer:
        print("Correct!")
        print(f"Guesses: {tries}")
        break
    elif guess > answer:
        print("Too high")
    else:
        print("Too low")
steps.explain: tries starts at 0 outside the loop and goes up by 1 with every number read. It's the same counting trick as "Adding up totals" in Chapter 5. Your game is done!
